changes: p4: name normalised to 'Jayasiṃhamalla' (stem without the -varman suffix, which is moved to titles); residence now given as Maṇigaṇa (Maṇigal) in Lalitapura; affiliation now covers both Ubhara-vihāra and the Thaula-vihāra kuṭumba
p3: confidence lowered to medium because the name 'Jayārjunadeva' is restored from the lacuna 'jaya..na'
p1: the 'guru' epithet is kept as written; added a note that Rāmadāsa is named as the author's father
date: ce_approx stays 1375 (Mārgaśira of NS 496 falls in Nov/Dec 1375; NS+880 would give 1376); explained in the notes

notes: The catalogue gives 'Jayasiṃha Malla (mahāpātra)' as king. That is wrong: Jayasiṃhamalla(varman) is the mahāpātra who owns the book. The reigning king is 'śrīśrījaya..na deva', most likely Jayārjunadeva (r. c. 1361–1382), but the name is restored from a lacuna. Rāmadāsa, the author's father, is called guru of the Nepal king's circle. He is not involved in this copy. Owner's locality: Maṇigaṇa (Maṇigal) in Lalitapura, and a kuṭumba of Ubhara-/Thaula-vihāra. The scribe's vihāra name is corrupt ('śrīyā..cchaṃ vihāralāṣṭhavastho'). Mārgaśira of NS 496 falls in late 1375 CE (NS+880 would give 1376).
